fullDesc: President Johnson signed the Voting Rights Act on August 6, 1965, after the Selma marches and the violence of Bloody Sunday. It banned practices like literacy tests that had kept Black citizens from voting.
realFacts: Black voter registration rose sharply in the South
The Selma marches were led by John Lewis, King and others
The Supreme Court weakened parts of it in 2013
Congress has renewed it several times
